Crown browse by type eq/excite/filter/wah wah wah fuzz-wah fuzz wah volume browse by enclosure treadle Crown FW-3 Distortion Wah Volume Published on October 1, 2015 Crown fuzz wah volume foot-controlled treadle Information The Crown FW-3 Distortion Wah Volume is a vintage analog multi-effect pedal produced in the United States by Applied Audio during the late 1960s and early 1970s. Distributed under several brand names including Guild, Atlantic, Kadent, Jax-USA, Lou Rose, Magnum, Nomad, and V-Jay, the Crown version shares identical circuitry with the Applied FW-3 and differs only in branding and minor cosmetic details. It integrates distortion, wah, and volume controls in a single treadle-operated enclosure and is recognized as one of the earliest examples of a multi-function effects pedal. The FW-3 features a robust cast-metal chassis with a steel treadle pedal that operates as both a wah controller and a passive volume pedal when the wah circuit is off. Two rotary controls adjust the output volume and the depth or intensity of the distortion effect. Dual mechanical footswitches independently activate the fuzz and wah sections. The distortion circuit delivers a buzzy, mid-focused fuzz typical of 1960s transistor-based designs, ranging from mild drive to rich, sustaining saturation. The wah circuit produces a broad, vocal sweep with a smooth, moderate resonance, shaped by a ferrite-core toroidal inductor that contributes to the pedal's characteristic warm tone. Internally, the Crown FW-3 uses a fully analog transistor circuit built on a printed circuit board (PCB). This PCB-based layout was standard across nearly all Applied Audio production units, with only a very small number of early Guild examples using handwired point-to-point construction. The circuit typically employs germanium or early silicon transistors depending on production batch, along with carbon-composition resistors and Stackpole potentiometers commonly dated around 1967. The pedal is powered by a single 9V battery (originally type 2U6) and uses mechanical footswitches for true mechanical engagement without buffering.
